fixes.find: still without a diploma, in my last year of correspondence school.
fixes.replace: still without a diploma, in my final year as a correspondence student.
fixes.why: “correspondence school” sounds like a separate school, not заочка at an institute.

fixes.find: a desk in the assignment room, by the window, where you can see the headframe.
fixes.replace: a desk in the shift office, by the window, where you can see the headframe.
fixes.why: “assignment room” is a literal калька; “shift office” reads naturally in the mine context.

fixes.find: who goes where, on what job, how many meters.
fixes.replace: who goes where, to do what, how many meters.
fixes.why: “on what job” is unidiomatic here.

fixes.find: two kids in paid colleges in Kemerovo.
fixes.replace: two kids in Kemerovo colleges, both paying tuition.
fixes.why: “paid colleges” sounds as if the colleges are paid/employed; the point is tuition.

fixes.find: Your Vitka's paying off a loan on his Lada.
fixes.replace: Your Vitka's paying off a loan on his Lada Nine.
fixes.why: Glossary keeps девятка as Lada Nine; plain Lada loses the specific realia.

fixes.find: It can only show me, too.
fixes.replace: It only knows how to show things, too.
fixes.why: The original echoes “I’m just showing you”; the English sentence is too cramped and unclear.

fixes.find: Vitka comes into the assignment room for his lamp, sees the bag and whistles.
fixes.replace: Vitka comes into the shift office for his lamp, sees the bag and whistles.
fixes.why: Same нарядная issue: “shift office” is idiomatic.

fixes.find: At the face he pulls it over the sensor and winds the tape, three turns, like a bandage.
fixes.replace: At the face he pulls it over the sensor and wraps the tape around it, three turns, like a bandage.
fixes.why: You wrap tape around something; “winds the tape” is missing the object.

fixes.find: From that bag on, everything went for me, as they say in the mine, on a level floor.
fixes.replace: From that bag on, as they say underground, I had level ground under me.
fixes.why: “everything went… on a level floor” is a literal translation that does not work as English.
fixes.replace_final: From that bag on, as they say underground, it was level going for me.

fixes.find: They haven't made me section chief yet that year, and that's worse than swearing.
fixes.replace: Back then I'm not section chief yet, and that makes it worse than swearing.
fixes.why: Present perfect plus “that year” is ungrammatical; present-tense narration can carry “back then.”

fixes.find: I say with the institute, by correspondence.
fixes.replace: I say I'm enrolled, by correspondence.
fixes.why: “with the institute” is a direct Russian construction, not English.

fixes.find: carries his pork fat to work in it.
fixes.replace: carries his salt pork to the shift in it.
fixes.why: “pork fat” is too raw/literal for сало in this context; “to the shift” also fits mine speech better.

fixes.find: Palych lay down on the rail at meter one hundred.
fixes.replace: Palych lay down on the rail at the hundred-meter mark.
fixes.why: “at meter one hundred” is Russian word order; “hundred-meter mark” is natural English.

fixes.find: That night I sat at the dispatcher's on the intercom, counting tags.
fixes.replace: That night I sat in the dispatcher's room at the intercom, counting tags.
fixes.why: “at the dispatcher’s” is an unidiomatic calque.

fixes.find: The door at the crosscut has been open for six days, propped with a prop, so they can haul timber faster.
fixes.replace: The door at the crosscut has been open for six days, held open with a roof prop, so they can haul timber faster.
fixes.why: “propped with a prop” is clumsy repetition.

fixes.find: somebody's propped it with a prop to haul timber faster.
fixes.replace: somebody's wedged it open with a roof prop to haul timber faster.
fixes.why: Avoids the same awkward repetition and clarifies the action.

fixes.find: The cold behind my ear stands still, like water in a barrel.
fixes.replace: The chill behind my ear stands still, like water in a barrel.
fixes.why: Glossary term for холодок is “the chill,” not “the cold.”

fixes.find: The door is propped with a prop.
fixes.replace: The door is held open with a roof prop.
fixes.why: Again, “propped with a prop” sounds accidentally comic.

fixes.find: I run along the drift, over the sleepers, in my self-rescuer, counting sleepers so I won't count minutes.
fixes.replace: I run along the drift, over the rail ties, in my self-rescuer, counting ties so I won't count minutes.
fixes.why: American spelling/style guide: “sleepers” is British; “rail ties” is clearer for a broad EN reader.

fixes.find: At the six hundredth sleeper smoke starts coming toward me, clear at first, then yellow.
fixes.replace: At the six hundredth tie smoke starts coming toward me, clear at first, then yellow.
fixes.why: Keeps terminology consistent with the previous fix.

fixes.find: The smoke is still standing in the drift, but no new smoke is coming.
fixes.replace: The smoke is still hanging in the drift, but no new smoke is coming.
fixes.why: Smoke “hangs” in English; “stands” is Russian interference.

fixes.find: He swallowed carbon monoxide while helping a young guy with his self-rescuer.
fixes.replace: He breathed in carbon monoxide while helping a young guy with his self-rescuer.
fixes.why: You inhale/breathe in carbon monoxide, not swallow it.

fixes.find: the third stall, the switch, the distribution point.
fixes.replace: the third recess, the switch, the distribution point.
fixes.why: Ниша in a mine passage is a recess/niche, not a stall.

fixes.find: I climb down along the frame to the walkway like off a stove.
fixes.replace: I climb down along the frame to the walkway, slow and careful.
fixes.why: “like off a stove” is opaque in English and distracts from the action.

fixes.find: The Glubokaya was closed in '26.
fixes.replace: The Glubokaya mine was closed in '26.
fixes.why: Glossary form is “the Glubokaya mine”; otherwise the name hangs unclear.

fixes.find: and this spoil heap is mine, by order, with a stamp.
fixes.replace: and this spoil heap is mine under an order with an official stamp on it.
fixes.why: “by order, with a stamp” is too literal; the legal-bureaucratic sense needs idiomatic English.

fixes.find: he said three sentences to me, one per breath:
fixes.replace: he said three things to me, one per breath:
fixes.why: “Three sentences” sounds grammatical/clinical; “three things” matches the Russian force better.

fixes.find: and his voice is torn, like in '96.
fixes.replace: and his voice is raw, like in '96.
fixes.why: A voice is “raw” or “hoarse” in English; “torn” is a literal Russian image.

fixes.find: by the fence with the sign "DANGER! BURNING WASTE DUMP,"
fixes.replace: by the fence with the sign "DANGER! BURNING SPOIL HEAP,"
fixes.why: “Waste dump” suggests a landfill; this is a mining spoil heap.

fixes.find: and under it nothing, and in that nothing it's six hundred degrees.
fixes.replace: and under it is empty space, six hundred degrees hot.
fixes.why: The literal repetition of “nothing” is awkward in English.

fixes.find: Dare you, don't dare you. In our yard that word drowned more kids than the current ever did.
fixes.replace: Chicken, not chicken. In our yard that word drowned more kids than the current ever did.
fixes.why: “Dare you, don’t dare you” is not what boys would say; “chicken” carries the dare.
fixes.replace_final: "Bet you can't." In our yard those words drowned more kids than the current ever did.

fixes.find: and heat blasts out like from a stove when you open the damper.
fixes.replace: and heat blasts out as if from a stove when you open the damper.
fixes.why: “like from” is ungrammatical here.

fixes.find: He grabs me with both hands, and I carry him down in my own tracks,
fixes.replace: He clings to me with both hands, and I carry him down along my own tracks,
fixes.why: “Clings” fits вцепляется; “in my own tracks” is not idiomatic for the route.

fixes.find: Look at your feet.
fixes.replace: Look down at your feet.
fixes.why: Natural command in this situation; the Russian means look under/down at them.

fixes.find: You won't help him, you'll go through,
fixes.replace: You won't help him, you'll break through,
fixes.why: The danger is breaking through the crust, not just “going through” in the abstract.

fixes.find: I go around the slope from the river side, into the wind, watching my feet.
fixes.replace: I go around the slope from the river side, into the wind, watching where I step.
fixes.why: English idiom is “watch where I step,” not “watch my feet.”

fixes.find: a sweater that costs as much as my Patriot SUV.
fixes.replace: a sweater that costs as much as my UAZ Patriot SUV.
fixes.why: “Patriot SUV” can read as generic/Western; the Russian realia is the UAZ Patriot.

fixes.find: At the bottom, a line for the chief engineer's signature. Mine.
fixes.replace: At the bottom is a line for the chief engineer's signature: mine.
fixes.why: The one-word dramatic sentence is an AI-ish beat; the colon is cleaner and drier.

fixes.find: and money the new owners won't give for it.
fixes.replace: and money the new owners won't spend on it.
fixes.why: In English owners spend money on work; they don’t “give money for it” in this context.

fixes.find: "The Kuzbass directorship opens up in January," says Arseny Olegovich, looking out the window.
fixes.replace: "The Kuzbass director's post opens up in January," says Arseny Olegovich, looking out the window.
fixes.why: “Directorship” is stiff and vague; he is offering a конкретная должность.

fixes.find: the way people ask "So, had the baby?"
fixes.replace: the way people ask, "So, have the baby yet?"
fixes.why: The colloquial English version of ну, родила? needs present perfect/“yet.”

fixes.find: Tanya is a caretaker at the museum on Krasnaya Gorka now;
fixes.replace: Tanya works as a museum attendant on Krasnaya Gorka now;
fixes.why: “Caretaker” suggests janitorial/building care; смотрительница is an attendant.

fixes.find: and counts them back in by heads.
fixes.replace: and collects them afterward, counting heads.
fixes.why: “By heads” is Russian interference; the action is counting children/helmets as they return.

fixes.find: "Put it out," he says. I say I put it out.
fixes.replace: "You put it out," he says. I say I did.
fixes.why: «Потушил» is a statement of completion, not an imperative.

fixes.find: and in winter the snow won't lie on it.
fixes.replace: and in winter snow doesn't lie on it.
fixes.why: For habitual physical fact, English wants present simple; “won’t lie” sounds like prediction or refusal.

verdict: Партия в целом сильная: техническая среда читается, взрослый голос держится сухо, важные развилки понятны. Чаще всего мешают буквальные русские конструкции (“with the institute,” “by heads,” “at meter one hundred”), шероховатая сочетаемость в бытовых фразах и отдельные потери реалий/глоссария вроде Lada Nine, UAZ Patriot и the chill. Самые опасные смысловые сбои — там, где английская фраза меняет модальность: “Put it out” как приказ вместо признания, “go through” вместо провалиться сквозь корку.
